additive_levers.attribution_limitation: a run recorded as SCHEDULED is invoked with the scheduler's own arguments, which is also what an on-demand `schtasks /run` does; the Task Scheduler operational log that would separate them is disabled on this host, so an off-phase launch is reported as off-phase and not attributed to a mechanism
additive_levers.what_start_when_available_buys: it converts a start missed while the host was unavailable into a catch-up run when the host returns; it does not help a start that could not run because no session existed, which is the loss this campaign is actually about

evaluations.question: an S4U task stores no password and runs with no session; needs the batch-logon right

evaluations.detail: no account in this inventory is designated for the lane, and granting a right to an existing account is a change to this host's policy, which this package does not make
evaluations.question: a designated account whose rights are granted for this purpose

evaluations.detail: creating a service needs administrator rights; a refused attempt can leave a half-created service behind, and this package does not change the host
evaluations.question: a service removes the session dependence and needs administrator rights to create

evaluations.detail: no SSH configuration, no known remote host and no self-hosted runner declaration was found in this checkout; a runner on another host stays a documented option for an operator who has one, not a mechanism this package can exercise
evaluations.question: a runner on another host, if authorised infrastructure exists

evaluations.detail: the LogonTrigger is additive: it does not remove the session absence, it bounds the recovery from it, and it is registered in the same scheduler the lane already uses
evaluations.question: a mitigation: it does not remove the absence, it bounds the recovery from it

selected_detail: the host refused the S4U registration of this very definition, so the mechanism that removes the dependence is not available to this process; the logon trigger is the strongest available one and is already exercised
selection_rule: prefer the mechanism that removes the dependence and stores no credential; fall back to the additive mechanism that bounds the loss instead of the one that would require a credential or a privilege this package does not have
